blocks.text: Rasulullaah ﷺ then said, 'You may either ride with me or go back.' I therefore went back."[^1]
The Incident of a man Who Sought Permission to Enter without first Greeting

Hadhrat Rib'ee bin Hiraash (RA) narrates from a man from the Banu Aamir tribe who once came to Rasulullaah ﷺ and asked, "May I come in?" Rasulullaah ﷺ said to a slave girl, "Go outside and tell him that he should say, 'اَلسَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ (As Salaamu Alaykum). May I come in?' he has certainly not done well in his asking permission to enter." The man however overheard this before the girl could some to him and said, "اَلسَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ (As Salaamu Alaykum). May I come in?" Rasulullaah ﷺ responded by saying, "وَعَلَيْكَ (Wa Alayk). You may now come in." The Hadith continues further.[^2]
Hadhrat Umar (RA), Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) and Hadhrat Ali (RA) Seek Permission to see Rasulullaah ﷺ

Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) reports that Hadhrat Umar (RA) once came to see Rasulullaah ﷺ in his upper storey room saying, "اَلسَّلَامُ عَلَيْكَ (As Salaamu Alayka) O Rasulullaah ﷺ! اَلسَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ (As Salaamu Alaykum). May Umar come in?"[^3]

blocks.arabic_text: اَلسَّلَامُ عَلَيْكَ أَيُّهَا النَّبِيُّ وَرَحْمَةُ اللّٰهِ وَبَرَكَاتُهٗ
blocks.text:
Another narration[^4] from Hadhrat Umar (RA) states that he said:
He then continued saying, "اَلسَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ (As Salaamu Alaykum). Can Umar come in?" In another narration[^5], Hadhrat Umar (RA) says that Rasulullaah ﷺ granted him permission to enter after he had asked thrice.
Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) narrates that when they once came to Rasulullaah ﷺ after he had sent for them, they first sought permission to enter.[^6]

Hadhrat Safeenah (RA) narrates that he was once with Rasulullaah ﷺ when Hadhrat Ali (RA) arrived, wanting to enter the room. As he knocked very lightly at the door, Rasulullaah ﷺ gave the instruction for the door to be opened for him.[^7]
